bio.en: Jeetu Patel is Chief Product Officer and President at Cisco, where he has led a remarkable internal transformation to make a traditionally slow enterprise giant operate in an AI-first way.
bio.zh: Jeetu Patel 是 Cisco 的首席产品官兼总裁，他在内部推动了一场显著的转型，让这家传统上偏慢的企业巨头以“AI 优先”的方式运作。

summary.en: Jeetu argues AI is a megatrend, not a hype cycle—one of the most foundational movements in human history—and that survival (think falling birth rates and caring for aging populations) may depend on successful AI. He shares how he's turning Cisco AI-first, why you should 'fast-forward six months' to prepare for the world to come, and why he rejects the 'praise in public, criticize in private' rule in favor of enough trust to debate in public. He also stresses that stamina trumps intellect—you can't teach hunger, curiosity, and persistence. The episode is a masterclass in leading change at enterprise scale.
summary.zh: Jeetu 主张 AI 是“大趋势”而非炒作周期——是人类历史上最具基础性的运动之一，并认为人类存续（想想下降的出生率与照护老龄人口）可能取决于 AI 的成功。他分享了如何把 Cisco 转型为 AI 优先、为何要“快进六个月”为未来的世界做准备，以及他为何反对“公开表扬、私下批评”、主张建立足够信任以公开辩论。他还强调“耐力胜过智力”——饥饿感、好奇心与毅力无法被教会。这期节目是关于在企业规模上领导变革的公开课。

turns.speaker: Jeetu Patel
turns.en: Survival of humanity depends on the successful AI. Birth rates are going down. If you have 60% of your population where you don't have enough people who take care of them, that could cause a lot of human suffering. When I got this new job, there's zero chance I would have been able to do it if AI wasn't there, because I didn't know anything about so many domains that we were in.
turns.zh: 人类的生存依赖于人工智能的成功。生育率正在下降。如果60%的人口缺乏能照顾他们的后代的人口，这可能会导致人类遭受巨大痛苦。当我获得这份新工作时，如果没有人工智能的支持，我绝对不可能胜任这份工作，因为我们所处的许多领域我都一无所知。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: A lot of companies are trying to adjust to this new world.
turns.zh: 许多公司正努力适应这个新世界。

turns.speaker: Jeetu Patel
turns.en: You have to know the difference between a megatrend and a hype cycle. When there's a megatrend, don't fight it. AI is a megatrend, one of the most foundational movements that we have seen in human history.
turns.zh: 你必须区分大趋势和炒作周期。当出现大趋势时，别与之对抗。人工智能就是大趋势，是人类历史上最具基础性的变革之一。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: To turn Cisco from an older, slower, more traditional enterprise to a very AI-forward company, this is very difficult to do.
turns.zh: 要将思科从一家老旧、缓慢、传统的企业转变为一家积极布局人工智能的公司，难度极大。

turns.speaker: Jeetu Patel
turns.en: AI is moving so fast. One of the things I tell my team is, "Fast-forward six months from now, get prepared for that world."
turns.zh: 人工智能发展极快。我常对团队说："快进六个月，从现在开始为那个世界做好准备。"

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You manage 30,000 people.
turns.zh: 你管理着3万名员工。

turns.speaker: Jeetu Patel
turns.en: Every management book that you read will tell you in public criticize in private. I fundamentally disagree with that notion. What you have to do is, is establish enough trust among the team so that you are comfortable critiquing and debating in public.
turns.zh: 你读过的每本管理书籍都会告诉你，要"公开表扬，私下批评"。我从根本上反对这种观点。你需要在团队中建立足够的信任，让大家能在公开场合坦然地提出批评和质疑。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What's something that you wish you'd known before taking on this role?
turns.zh: 担任这个职位之前，你希望自己能提前了解什么？

turns.speaker: Jeetu Patel
turns.en: Stamina trumps intellect. It's very important to have smart people, but you can become smart if you have curiosity and hunger and staying power and persistence. You can't teach hunger.
turns.zh: 耐力比智力更重要。拥有聪明的员工固然重要，但只要有好奇心、进取心、持久力和坚持力，你也可以变得聪明。求知若渴的渴望是无法教会的。

turns.speaker: Jeetu Patel
turns.en: It was an amazing thing to pull off, because we never thought we'd be able to do it, and we were really worried going into it, thinking, "Well, we're trying to do fireside chats for 12 hours, and there's a capacity of human absorption that we're trying to challenge." And so, we tried to put a lot of breaks in there and we started at nine a.m and we ended at nine p.m., and we had a couple hour break in the middle, but everyone stayed and everyone was engaged and we could have gone until 11 and it would've been fine. And it's because the quality of the conversations and the caliber of the guests that were there made a world of a difference. (00:05:53): What was the takeaway from it? I'd say a few things. One is the capabilities overhang is real. I think there's more functionality, on one end there's kind of this paradox of progress. On one end we are solving all these amazing problems with science, on the other end you talk to the enterprise, they're like, "We're struggling with adoption." And I feel like there's help that's going to be needed within organizations. And the reason we pulled this thing together, the goal was, what is happening in the industry and how can we help customers make sure that they can make the most of it? Because we are in one of the most foundational movements that we have seen in human history, and it's we got to make sure that we make the most of it. So, that was one is, the capabilities overhang is real. (00:06:37): The second area is, I'd say that it's harder when you go beyond some of the more obvious use cases. For example, coding is a very, very good use case that you're starting to get a lot of success in. I mean, we just had our first product that we think we'll be in the next two weeks, 100% written with AI. I don't think that's as easy when you go into every other function of the business. And that was actually very apparent that hey, this is going to require some nuance and understanding of how every business works. (00:07:10): And then the third one, which is a really interesting takeaway, and Marc Andreessen talked about this in your podcast a few days ago. In fact, when I talked to him, I actually started with your podcast, because it was so interesting, and then we dug into it a little bit more. And then Kevin Scott was also talking about this, but this notion of the fact that birth rates are going down and we have a demographic shift that's happening in the world and there's going to be more people that are in the older age bracket than the younger age bracket, and those older people are going to need folks to take care of them. (00:07:42): And historically in society, that's actually always been the case, but we might be at a point where that might not be the case. And when that's not the case, we worry about AI taking our jobs, I think that survival of humanity depends on a successful AI. So, I don't think people talk about this enough, and that's something that we have to take a moment and digest, that this is so important for our collective success moving forward.
turns.zh:
能成功举办这场活动真是令人惊叹，因为我们从未想过能做到这一点。在活动开始前，我们真的很担心，心想：“我们要连续12小时进行炉边谈话，而人类的接受能力是有限的。”因此，我们特意安排了多次休息时间——上午9点开始，晚上9点结束，中间有几个小时的休息，但所有人都全程参与，热情不减。即便延长到晚上11点也完全没问题。这一切都得益于对话的质量和嘉宾的水平所带来的巨大影响力。

（00:05:53）：那这次活动有什么收获呢？我总结了几点：首先，技术能力的供需失衡是真实存在的。一方面，我们通过科学解决了许多难题；另一方面，当与企业沟通时，他们却说：“我们在应用推广上遇到了困难。”我觉得企业内部需要获得帮助。举办这次活动的初衷，就是要了解行业现状，帮助客户充分利用新技术。我们身处人类历史上最具变革性的时代之一，必须确保能充分把握机遇。

（00:06:37）：第二点是，当你超越那些显而易见的应用场景时，挑战会更大。比如编程领域已经取得了巨大成功，我们刚刚推出了首款100%由AI编写的产品。但将AI应用于其他业务场景时，难度会显著增加。这充分说明，我们需要深入理解各行业的运作机制。

（00:07:10）：第三点启发来自马克·安德森几天前在播客中的论述。实际上，我和他交谈时也是从你的播客入手的，因为内容太引人入胜了。凯文·斯科特也谈到了出生率下降带来的人口结构变化——未来老年人口将超过年轻群体，而这些老年人需要他人照料。历史上这种现象一直存在，但现在可能面临转折。当这种平衡被打破时，人们会担忧AI会抢走工作机会。但我认为人类的生存依赖于AI的成功应用。若60%的人口处于缺乏照料的年龄段，人类将面临巨大挑战。因此，这个问题值得我们深思熟虑，它对我们未来的集体成功至关重要。

turns.speaker: Lenny

In my head I was thinking, "This is like another signal that we are in a simulation that things are working out just right for us." What are the chances?
turns.zh: 之前在和马克聊天时，他提到人工智能的到来恰好拯救了我们，因为劳动力短缺导致职位空缺无法填补。这时我脑海中浮现："这仿佛又在暗示，我们身处一个精心设计的模拟世界，一切都在为我们量身打造。这种可能性有多大？"

turns.speaker: Jeetu Patel
turns.en: The older I get, the more I believe that we are actually in a simulation. The first time I heard that concept, I thought it was such an absurd concept. Now I'm like, "This might actually be happening." You never know.
turns.zh: 随着年龄增长，我愈发坚信我们确实生活在一个模拟世界中。初次听闻这个概念时，我觉得它荒谬至极。如今我却会想："这或许真有可能发生。"世事难料。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Following this thread, a lot of companies are trying to adjust to this new world. You are doing an incredible job at actually doing this. We got connected through Kevin Weil, who is former CPO at OpenAI, now head of science at OpenAI. How many employees do you guys have? You said 45,000.
turns.zh: 围绕这个话题，许多公司正努力适应新环境。你们在这方面做得非常出色。我们通过OpenAI前首席产品官、现任科学主管凯文·韦尔结缘。他向我们描述了你们将思科从传统、缓慢的企业转变为AI先锋公司的历程。你们有多少员工？你提到过45,000人。

turns.speaker: Jeetu Patel
turns.en: We have 90,000 employees, 43,000 watch the stream.
